prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1109; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival in Pearland, Texas, I found a rear-end collision involving two vehicles. Driver 1 was stopped in the travel lane when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of it. Driver 2 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash and said they were seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. I confirmed that Driver 2 was present in the vehicle when I arrived. The damage to both vehicles lines up with the impact described by the drivers, and the reported injury fits the force of a collision of this type. Scene photographs show several of the details the parties described. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the statements of the drivers, the Passenger, and the physical evidence. Driver 1 is the named insured on the policy for the vehicle they were operating. Neither driver reported any prior damage to their vehicle, and none was visible during the inspection. The Passenger reported no injuries at the scene. Both drivers were cooperative, and I issued the citation described in the attached supplement.
